raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Purpose

- Resolves #51868: adaptive verification needs Mamba decode batches with per-request query lengths
- Audit: the Mamba2 decode kernels already handle ragged batches from device offsets, so this is wiring only
- Flip `supports_device_cpu_query_lens_mismatch` on Mamba2; ReplaySSM still opts out
- Keep `UNIFORM_BATCH`; bound varlen FULL decode graphs via `get_varlen_cudagraph_max_query_len` = `max_decode_query_len` (#57263)
- Not a duplicate: no open PR touches Mamba varlen decode

## Test Plan

- `pytest tests/kernels/mamba/test_causal_conv1d.py` with new ragged-varlen test + uniform regression (L4)
- SSU ragged coverage already exists upstream
- Kernel perf: ragged/trimmed vs uniform-padded at Nemotron-H shapes (B200)
- E2E: Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B + MTP k=8, AV on/off, GSM8K 200 (B200)

## Test Result

- 146 passed, 0 failed

| batch | max_q | case | tokens | conv_us | ssu_us | total_us | vs uniform |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 8 | 8 | uniform | 64 | 37.8 | 90.1 | 127.9 | 1.00 |
| 8 | 8 | ragged q~U[1,8] | 42 | 36.2 | 89.5 | 125.7 | 0.98 |
| 8 | 8 | trimmed to 1 | 8 | 35.2 | 83.0 | 118.2 | 0.92 |
| 32 | 4 | uniform | 128 | 36.0 | 186.4 | 222.4 | 1.00 |
| 32 | 4 | ragged q~U[1,4] | 83 | 35.9 | 141.2 | 177.1 | 0.80 |
| 32 | 4 | trimmed to 1 | 32 | 36.0 | 90.3 | 126.4 | 0.57 |
| 32 | 8 | uniform | 256 | 35.2 | 334.9 | 370.0 | 1.00 |
| 32 | 8 | ragged q~U[1,8] | 151 | 35.1 | 227.7 | 262.7 | 0.71 |
| 32 | 8 | trimmed to 1 | 32 | 36.5 | 89.4 | 125.9 | 0.34 |
| 128 | 8 | uniform | 1024 | 33.8 | 1296.8 | 1330.5 | 1.00 |
| 128 | 8 | ragged q~U[1,8] | 596 | 33.9 | 866.1 | 900.0 | 0.68 |
| 128 | 8 | trimmed to 1 | 128 | 36.1 | 286.9 | 323.0 | 0.24 |

- No fixed varlen overhead (unlike #52157): trimmed batches cut SSU time token-linearly
- E2E GSM8K 200: AV 181, no-AV 184; FULL decode graphs captured in both

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used; every changed line was reviewed by the submitter.

---

nodes.body: Hi @benchislett could you also help take a look at this one, thanks!

Do you have results from nemotron + AV? Something like:

```shell
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 \
  vllm serve nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B-BF16 \
    --attention-backend TRITON_ATTN \
    --speculative-config '{
      "method": "mtp",
      "num_speculative_tokens": 8,
      "enable_adaptive_verification": true
    }'
```

Hi @tomasruizt Just ran your command on B200 (V2 runner, TRITON_ATTN, MTP k=8, this PR on top of 88aa0d287d).

Without this PR, startup fails: `Adaptive verification trims verification requests on device, which the Mamba2AttentionBackend attention backend does not support.` With this PR it serves correctly. GSM8K 200q: 191/200 with AV vs 190/200 without.

Throughput with GSM8K prompts, max_tokens 512, average of 2 runs (out tok/s, AV vs no AV):

| conc | AV | no AV | diff | mean accept len (AV / no AV) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 669 | 722 | -7% | 5.24 / 5.44 |
| 8 | 2597 | 2677 | -3% | 5.40 / 5.48 |
| 32 | 4935 | 6211 | -21% | 5.21 / 5.37 |
| 64 | 9707 | 8931 | +9% | 5.09 / 5.40 |
| 128 | 14876 | 12112 | +23% | 4.95 / 5.42 |

The direction is consistent across both runs, but the magnitude is noisy. AV helps at high concurrency and costs a bit at low/mid concurrency. I have not checked whether the conc 32 dip is specific to Mamba, or whether AV with MTP does the same on a pure-attention model.

Hi @guan404ming! I ran the benchmarks using a DSpark drafter instead (https://huggingface.co/nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B-NVFP4-DSpark). In general I measured approximate parity with not using AV on low batch sizes (a ~3.6% degradation at bsz=32, K=7), and a speedups at bsz > 128. The speedups are more consistent at K=15. Full report: https://tomasruizt.github.io/reports/nemotron-3.5-dspark-av/

Thanks @tomasruizt, great to have an independent run.

I think the direction matches my B200 MTP k=8 numbers: flat at low concurrency, gains at high, acceptance length unchanged. The conc 32 dip I saw does not reproduce with DSpark, so it is likely noise or MTP-specific rather than a Mamba varlen issue.

This pull request has merge conflicts that must be resolved before it can be
merged. Please rebase the PR, @guan404ming.

https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/working-with-forks/syncing-a-fork

The test makes sense to me. I suggest to factor out helper functions to make the structure clearer: we are comparing the batched varlen state update against individual calls (the reference). Here is a suggestion: https://github.com/tomasruizt/vllm/commit/a91e19677ec7379f6a2661a384d8bce033c3eb84
Thanks, applied in f83280feef (dropped the docstrings, cast the offsets to int). Also rebased on main.

Done in 6efb6cb752: kept UNIFORM_BATCH and added get_varlen_cudagraph_max_query_len on the Mamba2 builder. Also dropped the relaxed assert and the builder ReplaySSM check, since the AV startup check already covers ReplaySSM. B200 GSM8K 200: AV 181, no-AV 184.

@guan404ming it looks like the kernel failures are related
```
FAILED tests/kernels/mamba/test_causal_conv1d.py::test_causal_conv1d_update_ragged_varlen[q_lens_cfg1-64-4-True-True-itype0]
FAILED tests/kernels/mamba/test_causal_conv1d.py::test_causal_conv1d_update_ragged_varlen[q_lens_cfg0-64-4-True-True-itype0]
```
Thanks, fixed in 36abcd3d93. The CPU kernel ignores `num_accepted_tokens`, so I skipped the test on CPU.

✅ Triggered [Buildkite CI #95422](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/95422) for commit `9bc1d7313bf1`.

ℹ️ This PR is 5 commits behind upstream `main`. Merged upstream `main` into this branch as `9bc1d7313bf1` before starting CI. Pull the branch before pushing more changes.

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

Thanks, the decode path looks correct and it validated cleanly on my end (GSM8K matches with/without AV on Nemotron-3.5-Lightning + MTP k=8, B300).

One change before merging: please don't report `AttentionCGSupport.ALWAYS` from `get_cudagraph_support`. Mamba can't run mixed prefill batches in FULL graphs; this only works today because adaptive verification forces FULL_AND_PIECEWISE.

#57263 added `get_varlen_cudagraph_max_query_len` for this case. Please:
- Drop the `get_cudagraph_support` override and keep `UNIFORM_BATCH`.
- Override `get_varlen_cudagraph_max_query_len` on the Mamba2 builder to return `max_decode_query_len(vllm_config)` (see `FlashInferMLASparseTRTLLMMetadataBuilder`).
- Drop the relaxed assert in `build_for_cudagraph_capture` if it's no longer needed (varlen capture passes `max_query_len = decode_query_len`).

@@ -2,6 +2,8 @@
 # SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
 
 
+from collections.abc import Iterator
+
 import pytest
 import torch
 import torch.nn.functional as F
@@ -358,3 +360,113 @@ def test_causal_conv1d_varlen(
     )
     unpadded_out = out[:, : out_ref_tensor.shape[-1]]
     assert torch.allclose(unpadded_out, out_ref_tensor, rtol=rtol, atol=atol)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("itype", [torch.bfloat16])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("silu_activation", [True])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("has_bias", [True])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("width", [4])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("dim", [64, 2048])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("q_lens_cfg", [[3, 1, 0, 4, 2], [1, 5, 5, 1], [2, 0, 0, 3]])
+@pytest.mark.skipif(
+    current_platform.is_cpu(),
+    reason="CPU kernel for causal_conv1d_update ignores num_accepted_tokens.",
+)
+def test_causal_conv1d_update_ragged_varlen(
+    q_lens_cfg, dim, width, has_bias, silu_activation, itype
+):
+    mk_inputs = lambda: _create_ragged_varlen_inputs(
+        q_lens_cfg, dim, width, has_bias, silu_activation, itype
+    )
+    inputs, state = mk_inputs()
+    actual = causal_conv1d_update(conv_state=state, **inputs)
+
+    ref_inputs, ref_state = mk_inputs()
+    ref_outs = _create_ragged_varlen_ref_outs(conv_state=ref_state, **ref_inputs)
+
+    for i, ref_out in enumerate(ref_outs):
+        start = int(inputs["query_start_loc"][i])
+        end = int(inputs["query_start_loc"][i + 1])
+        entry = inputs["conv_state_indices"][i : i + 1]
+        assert torch.allclose(actual[start:end], ref_out, rtol=1e-2, atol=5e-2)
+        assert torch.equal(state[entry], ref_state[entry])
+
+
+def _create_ragged_varlen_inputs(
+    q_lens_cfg, dim, width, has_bias, silu_activation, itype
+):
+    device = DEVICE
+    set_random_seed(0)
+
+    batch_size = len(q_lens_cfg)
+    max_query_len = 5
+    assert max(q_lens_cfg) <= max_query_len
+    state_len = width - 1 + max_query_len
+    total_entries = 10 * batch_size
+
+    q_lens = torch.tensor(q_lens_cfg, dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
+    query_start_loc = torch.cat(
+        [
+            torch.zeros(1, dtype=torch.int32, device=device),
+            torch.cumsum(q_lens, dim=0, dtype=torch.int32),
+        ]
+    )
+    total_tokens = int(q_lens.sum())
+
+    x = torch.randn(total_tokens, dim, device=device, dtype=itype)
+    conv_state = torch.randn(
+        total_entries, state_len, dim, device=device, dtype=itype
+    ).transpose(1, 2)
+    weight = torch.randn(dim, width, device=device, dtype=itype)
+    bias = torch.randn(dim, device=device, dtype=itype) if has_bias else None
+    activation = None if not silu_activation else "silu"
+
+    conv_state_indices = (
+        torch.randperm(total_entries - 1, device=device)[:batch_size] + 1
+    ).to(torch.int32)
+    num_accepted_tokens = torch.randint(
+        1, max_query_len + 1, (batch_size,), dtype=torch.int32, device=device
+    )
+    inputs = dict(
+        x=x,
+        weight=weight,
+        bias=bias,
+        activation=activation,
+        conv_state_indices=conv_state_indices,
+        num_accepted_tokens=num_accepted_tokens,
+        query_start_loc=query_start_loc,
+        max_query_len=max_query_len,
+    )
+    return inputs, conv_state
+
+
+def _create_ragged_varlen_ref_outs(
+    x,
+    conv_state,
+    weight,
+    bias,
+    activation,
+    conv_state_indices,
+    num_accepted_tokens,
+    query_start_loc,
+    max_query_len,
+) -> Iterator[torch.Tensor]:
+    for seq_idx in range(len(conv_state_indices)):
+        start = int(query_start_loc[seq_idx])
+        end = int(query_start_loc[seq_idx + 1])
+        entry = conv_state_indices[seq_idx : seq_idx + 1]
+        if start == end:
+            yield x[start:end]
+            continue
+        out_ref = causal_conv1d_update(
+            x[start:end],
+            conv_state,
+            weight,
+            bias,
+            activation=activation,
+            conv_state_indices=entry,
+            num_accepted_tokens=num_accepted_tokens[seq_idx : seq_idx + 1],
+            query_start_loc=query_start_loc.new_tensor([0, end - start]),
+            max_query_len=max_query_len,
+        )
+        yield out_ref

+from vllm.config import VllmConfig, get_current_vllm_config_or_none
 from vllm.model_executor.layers.mamba.checkpoint import (
     MambaPrefillCheckpointBuilder,
     MambaPrefillCheckpointMetadata,
@@ -15,12 +15,13 @@

     AttentionBackend,
     CommonAttentionMetadata,
+    max_decode_query_len,
 )
 from vllm.v1.attention.backends.mamba_attn import (
     BaseMambaAttentionMetadata,
     BaseMambaAttentionMetadataBuilder,
 )
-from vllm.v1.kv_cache_interface import MambaSpec
+from vllm.v1.kv_cache_interface import KVCacheSpec, MambaSpec
 
 
 def compute_varlen_chunk_metadata(
@@ -104,6 +105,14 @@ def get_builder_cls() -> type["Mamba2AttentionMetadataBuilder"]:
     def is_ssm(cls) -> bool:
         return True
 
+    @classmethod
+    def supports_device_cpu_query_lens_mismatch(cls) -> bool:
+        # Decode kernels take device offsets; ReplaySSM plans off CPU counts.
+        vllm_config = get_current_vllm_config_or_none()
+        if vllm_config is None:
+            return True
+        return not vllm_config.cache_config.use_replayssm
+
 
 @dataclass
 class Mamba2AttentionMetadata(BaseMambaAttentionMetadata):
@@ -124,6 +133,14 @@ class Mamba2AttentionMetadataBuilder(
 ):
     metadata_cls = Mamba2AttentionMetadata
 
+    @classmethod
+    def get_varlen_cudagraph_max_query_len(
+        cls,
+        vllm_config: VllmConfig,
+        kv_cache_spec: KVCacheSpec,
+    ) -> int | None:
+        return max_decode_query_len(vllm_config)
+
     def __init__(
         self,
         kv_cache_spec: MambaSpec,
